correctness.rationale: The exact stretch-time substitution has zero symbolic residual. The four rectangle faces have the signed inward margins k(eta/2-eta^2), -k(eta/2+eta^2), (d/2)(eta/2+3eta^2/2), (d/2)(-eta/2+3eta^2/2), all strict at 0<eta<1/3 after choosing x sufficiently large to absorb the uniformly decaying remainder. Thus the tube is invariant and x grows between two linear functions of stretched time; integrating dt/dtau=e^{-x/3} yields finite physical lifespan and the stated two-sided duration bounds. The explicit positive quadratic W=2h^2u^2/9+v^2 has the stated exact derivative and admits W'<=-gamma W+E^2/gamma; E decays exponentially, so scaled variables converge to the unique positive limiting sink. Integration of dq/dt=-Y/3 gives the physical logarithmic and derivative rates. Reflection proves the negative branch. Algebra checked with embedded verify.py; finite numerical examples are not used for completeness or asymptotics.

value.rationale: The motivating dissipative chaos paper makes a global-confinement inference from constant negative divergence. Open finite-time runaway basins for all positive damping c demonstrate why divergence cannot establish global boundedness. The exact time-to-blow-up brackets and universal coefficient log(12/d) and derivative rates 3,3 give mathematically informative asymptotic boundaries on the same dynamical system, not a narrow arbitrary example or a routine tabulation. The theorem complements (rather than duplicates) known compact-recurrence and local-bifurcation analysis, while not claiming to invalidate bounded attractors.
